name: Isla Nublar
region: Pacific Ocean, 190 km west of Costa Rica
terrain: Mountainous interior, coastal lowland, dense primary rainforest
climate: Tropical, high rainfall, seasonal storm exposure
established: 1982 — leased from the Costa Rican government
primaryFunction: Public exhibition of genetic assets; primary revenue site
description: The island InGen built its public face on. Nublar carried two complete park builds across three decades, and the second was more successful than the company has ever admitted in writing: Jurassic World operated at scale, profitably, for a decade. The site's defining weakness was never the animals. It was that every containment decision was made downstream of a guest-experience decision.
inGenInvolvement: Total. Site survey, land lease, infrastructure, both park builds, all asset transfers and both evacuations were InGen or Masrani Global operations.
historicalNotes: Mount Sibo was logged as dormant in the 1982 survey and never re-assessed. The 2018 eruption destroyed the site and every structure on it. The lease was not renewed; there is nothing left to renew.
notes: Site is a total loss. No recovery operations are authorised. Records retained for liability and research continuity only.

name: Isla Sorna
region: Las Cinco Muertes archipelago, Pacific Ocean
environment: Tropical island, larger and wetter than Nublar
terrain: River valleys, interior grassland, coastal cliff, heavy canopy
climate: Tropical, extreme rainfall, direct storm path
primaryFunction: Genetic production, incubation, rearing to viability, transfer staging
description: Every asset that ever walked on Nublar was made here first. Sorna was the factory floor: hatcheries, rearing paddocks, and the infrastructure to move a juvenile animal to exhibition once it was stable. Hurricane Clarissa ended staffed operations in 1995 and personnel left in days, releasing assets rather than destroying them.
inGenInvolvement: Total, and deliberately undocumented. Sorna does not appear in investor material from the period; it appears in shipping manifests.
historicalNotes: The unplanned outcome is the most valuable thing in this file. Assets left to themselves bred, established territory and produced a functioning multi-generational ecosystem without human management. No InGen programme ever reproduced that result under controlled conditions.
notes: Site remains uncontained. Landing is prohibited under the 1998 accords. Observation continues by air at range.

name: Jurassic Park
region: Isla Nublar, southern and central sectors
environment: Constructed park within tropical island interior
terrain: Engineered enclosures, service road network, perimeter fencing
description: The original build, and the more ambitious of the two. Its enclosures were larger, its animal density lower, and its infrastructure almost entirely dependent on a single automated control system. It never sold a ticket. The endorsement inspection of June 1993 was intended to satisfy the underwriters; it ended with three fatalities and the site abandoned inside a week.
inGenInvolvement: Direct. Conceived, financed and built by InGen under John Hammond.
historicalNotes: The failure was structural, not zoological. A single unaudited engineer held root access to every door, fence and camera on the island, and the system had no manual fallback. The animals behaved exactly as their files predicted.
notes: Superseded by the Jurassic World build on the same island. Structures were partially reclaimed by forest before the 2018 event destroyed them.

name: Jurassic World
environment: Full resort complex within tropical island
terrain: Engineered lagoon, paddock network, urban resort core, monorail corridor
primaryFunction: Mass-market exhibition, resort operations, live attraction programming
description: What Hammond intended, delivered by people who understood throughput. Twenty thousand guests daily, a resort core with hotels and retail, and a paddock network built to move animals rather than merely hold them. It worked for ten years. The commercial machinery that made it work is also what produced the Indominus rex programme: attendance flattened, and the response was to engineer a bigger attraction.
inGenInvolvement: InGen operated as the genetics division under Masrani Global ownership throughout.
historicalNotes: The 2015 failure originated in the asset, not the infrastructure. Indominus rex defeated its enclosure using capabilities its own file did not record, because the file was written by the division that created it.
notes: Evacuated 2015, never reopened. Destroyed with the rest of the island in 2018.

name: Lockwood Estate
primaryFunction: Private archive; latterly unauthorised asset holding and auction
description: Benjamin Lockwood's home, and the place where InGen's founding work actually began — the sub-level laboratories predate anything on Nublar. In 2018 those same sub-levels were used to hold assets recovered from Isla Nublar for private sale, without the estate owner's knowledge or consent.
inGenInvolvement: Historic and foundational. Lockwood co-funded the original de-extinction research; the estate housed the first viable programme.
historicalNotes: The 2018 auction is the single largest uncontrolled dispersal of InGen genetic assets on record. Buyers were private and international. Most assets have never been recovered or located.
notes: Assets released into the surrounding region during the incident. Estate is no longer a secure site under any definition.

name: Biosyn Valley Sanctuary
terrain: Steep valley walls, forest floor, river system, sinkhole cave network
primaryFunction: Asset containment, research access, genetic study under sanctuary framing
description: A competitor's answer to the dispersal problem: a valley with walls high enough to act as a fence, presented to regulators as a sanctuary and operated as a research site. The framing is doing considerable work. The containment is real, the science is real, and so is the fact that Biosyn holds the largest concentrated population of InGen-derived assets outside Isla Sorna.
inGenInvolvement: None operationally. InGen assets present were acquired after the 2018 dispersal, not transferred.
historicalNotes: The 2022 events here concerned an agricultural pathogen programme, not the assets. The animals were incidental to what was actually being tested.
notes: Competitor site. Retained in this archive because a substantial share of InGen genetic material is held there.

name: Île Saint-Hubert
terrain: Coastal shelf, interior plateau, cliff perimeter
primaryFunction: Restricted genetic research beyond exhibition-viable parameters
description: The site that existed because Nublar and Sorna had to answer to visitors and inspectors. Saint-Hubert answered to neither. Work here ran past the point where an asset needed to be presentable, and several specimens on file were never intended to leave the island in any condition.
inGenInvolvement: Total, and deliberately unrecorded in corporate filings.
historicalNotes: The 2010 incident ended staffed operations. Assets were not recovered and were not destroyed. The island retains a viable population.
notes: Access requires Level 5 authorisation. No landing has been authorised since 2010.

name: Nublar Northern Sector
region: Isla Nublar, north of the resort perimeter
terrain: Ravines, dense canopy, decommissioned service roads
established: 2004 — designated during the Jurassic World build
primaryFunction: Asset holding away from guest sightlines; disposal of superseded infrastructure
description: The part of the island that guests were told did not exist. Sector 5 held the paddocks that could not be made presentable, the remains of the 1993 build, and any asset whose behavioural profile made it unsuitable for exhibition. Most of the Indominus rex programme was carried out here.
inGenInvolvement: Direct. Sector 5 was the operational reason the northern perimeter existed.
historicalNotes: Both major Nublar containment failures began in this sector. That is not coincidence — it is where the animals that could not be shown were kept.
notes: Destroyed with the island. Sector maps retained for incident reconstruction.

name: Jurassic World Lagoon
environment: Engineered saltwater basin with open-ocean exchange
terrain: Excavated basin, tiered spectator terracing, submerged containment grid
primaryFunction: Marine asset containment and public feeding exhibition
description: The largest single enclosure InGen ever built, and the only one designed around a feeding display. The basin exchanged water with the open ocean through a filtered channel — a decision that made husbandry viable and containment permanently conditional. When the island fell, the barrier was the only thing between the resident asset and the Pacific.
inGenInvolvement: Design consultation and asset provision; operated by Masrani Global.
historicalNotes: The lagoon's occupant remained contained through the 2015 incident and was the only exhibited asset to leave Nublar under its own power in 2018.
notes: Barrier integrity failed during the 2018 evacuation. Asset is at large in the Pacific.

name: Sorna Interior Basin
environment: Open grassland bounded by rainforest and river
terrain: Alluvial plain, braided river channels, cliff margins
established: Not constructed — formed after the 1995 evacuation
description: The most scientifically valuable location in this archive, and the only one InGen did not build. When Sorna's staff left, the animals distributed themselves across the interior and sorted into a stable ecology: herd species on the plain, predators along the tree line, nesting sites on the higher ground. Every attempt to reproduce this behaviour inside a managed enclosure has failed.
historicalNotes: Both the 1997 and 2001 incidents involved parties entering this basin. Neither expedition was authorised by InGen, and both confirmed the same finding: the ecosystem is self-sustaining and does not require us.
notes: No landing authorised. Observation flights maintain 500 m minimum altitude.

name: InGen Corporate Headquarters
terrain: Constructed campus, three buildings, secure sub-level records store
primaryFunction: Corporate administration, legal, records custody, archive infrastructure
description: Where the paperwork lives. Every lease, manifest, incident report and personnel file in this archive is held or mirrored here, including the material that was never submitted to any regulator. Following the Masrani acquisition the campus retained records custody even as operational control moved offshore.
historicalNotes: The 1993 industrial espionage loss originated from an embedded contractor working out of this campus, not from Isla Nublar. The recovery of that material was never completed.
notes: This archive is served from this site. Access is logged.

name: Mantah Corp Island
environment: Small tropical island; single causeway approach
terrain: Low rock shelf and scrub over a raised coral platform, with an interior freshwater lagoon
primaryFunction: Private asset holding and behavioural experimentation
description: A competitor site holding InGen-derived assets acquired outside any transfer agreement. The survey plate shows a compact island reached by a single causeway, with one low-profile structure set into the rock above an interior lagoon and no visible secondary landing point. For a holding of its assessed value the footprint is small and the approach is narrow, which reads as a site built to be controlled rather than expanded. What is done there has never been established from open sources.
inGenInvolvement: None. Assets present are believed to originate from Isla Sorna without authorisation.
historicalNotes: Behavioural manipulation using implanted control devices is documented in recovered material. No InGen programme has ever authorised such work. The assets held here are assessed as Site B stock removed without agreement, which is the only established link between this site and InGen. The single causeway is the only route on or off the island identified in survey.
notes: Intelligence file. Contents are assessed, not verified. Position unconfirmed.
